idea: A booking page for a small yoga studio.
intro: I love getting the journey right before anyone draws a screen.

decision: What the confirm step asks the customer for
options: Name and email only, pay at the studio
Name, email and card payment up front
Require an account to sign in first
recommendation: Name and email only, pay at the studio
reason: The smallest version that works end to end avoids payment and accounts, and you can add them once you see evidence they are needed.

decision: What happens when a class is full
options: Show it as full with no booking
Offer a waitlist
Hide full classes
recommendation: Show it as full with no booking
reason: A waitlist is an extra that can wait for evidence, while showing the class as full is honest and cheap.

decision: Who 'Book your usual' serves and how it recognises a returning customer
options: Defer it until there is booking history to learn from
Remember the customer by email and offer their last class
Let them pick a saved favourite class
recommendation: Defer it until there is booking history to learn from
reason: It needs repeat-booking data to work and the first version should be proven end to end before adding a shortcut.

decision: How customers cancel or change a booking, and what the booked screen promises
options: Booked screen says to email or contact the studio to cancel
Self-serve cancel link in the confirmation, with a cutoff time
No cancellation mentioned
recommendation: Booked screen says to email or contact the studio to cancel
reason: A cancellation promise on the booked screen is hard to take back, and contacting the studio keeps v1 small while still covering the edge case.

note: Drafted the key journey decisions for the yoga studio booking page: payment and account at confirm, full classes, the "Book your usual" shortcut, and cancellations.

decision: Whether the booking page takes payment online or leaves it to the desk
options: Pay online when booking
Pay at the desk, page only reserves
Either: online or at the desk
recommendation: Pay online when booking
reason: Taking payment at the confirm step makes the booking work end to end and stops no-shows from costing the studio a seat.

decision: What people buy: single classes, class packs, or a monthly pass
options: Single classes only
Single classes plus a class pack
Single, pack and monthly membership
recommendation: Single classes plus a class pack
reason: A pack gives regulars a reason to come back, and "Book your usual" needs no membership billing to work.

decision: Cancellation and late-cancel rule: refund, credit or nothing back
options: Full refund up to a cutoff, none after
Credit back to the account, never cash
No refunds, only studio-cancelled classes are refunded
recommendation: Full refund up to a cutoff, none after
reason: A clear cutoff frees the seat for someone else and is a promise the customer sees before paying, so it has to be settled now.

decision: How classes are priced: one flat price or by class type, plus an intro offer
options: One flat price for every class
Price by class type (e.g. workshop vs regular)
Flat price plus a first-class intro offer
recommendation: One flat price for every class
reason: The smallest version needs one number to show and charge, and extra pricing can wait until there is evidence.

note: Pricing and payment choices for the yoga booking page: what a booking costs, how people pay, whether a spot is held with money, and what happens on cancellation.

decision: Whether full classes get a waitlist
options: Waitlist on full classes
Show 'full' only, no waitlist
Waitlist later, after evidence
recommendation: Show 'full' only, no waitlist
reason: One leisure centre (Active Monash) runs a waitlist and closes cancellations 1 hour before start, but that page was not opened and there are no figures on how often waitlisted people get in, so for a small studio's first version it can wait.

source.title: A public leisure centre runs a waitlist on full group-fitness classes
source.label: researched before the demo
source.how_verified: Seen in a web search result summary on 14 Nov 2026; the page itself could not be opened from the build session (host not reachable). Open the link to check before relying on it.

decision: What 'Book your usual' repeats (same class and time, or just the same class type)
options: Same class type, next available slot
Same class and weekday/time
Drop it from the first version
recommendation: Drop it from the first version
reason: We have no evidence yet that regulars rebook the same slot, so we'd learn first how members actually book before building a shortcut, and it matches shipping the smallest end-to-end version.

decision: Whether people book as guests or must create an account
options: Guest booking with name and email
Account required
Guest first, accounts later
recommendation: Guest booking with name and email
reason: We'd learn first whether the studio's customers mostly come back, and guest booking keeps the confirm step short while still capturing contact details.

decision: Whether payment is taken at booking or at the studio
options: Pay at booking
Pay at the studio
Booking only, payment handled outside the page
recommendation: Booking only, payment handled outside the page
reason: We'd learn first how the studio takes money today (drop-ins, packs, memberships) before building payment, since taking money is a promise that can't be cleanly undone.

note: Listed the four real decisions for the yoga studio booking page, with the waitlist one resting on the single pre-demo finding (unverified link) and the rest framed as what we'd learn first.

decision: What single number says the booking page worked
options: Share of class-list visitors who reach 'booked'
Total bookings per week
Share of bookings that are repeat 'Book your usual'
recommendation: Total bookings per week
reason: A raw weekly booking count is simple to read for a small studio and directly shows whether the page replaces manual booking.

decision: What to measure at the confirm step
options: Count confirm views that end in a booked event (drop-off rate)
Time spent on the confirm screen
Nothing beyond booked count
recommendation: Count confirm views that end in a booked event (drop-off rate)
reason: The confirm-to-booked drop-off is the clearest sign that the step is failing, and it needs just two events.

decision: What to keep from each booking at the booked step
options: Class id, timestamp and an anonymous client id only
Above plus name and email
Above plus name, email and payment details
recommendation: Above plus name and email
reason: The studio needs a name and email to confirm and contact the attendee, and payment details should stay with the payment provider rather than in our data.

decision: How to measure 'Book your usual' from the classes list
options: Count taps on 'Book your usual' that lead to a booking
Count taps only
Skip measuring until the shortcut has real use
recommendation: Count taps on 'Book your usual' that lead to a booking
reason: Tap-to-booking conversion tells us whether the shortcut is worth keeping and compares it with the longer path via a class page.

note: Picked one measure per journey box plus the whole-page success number, keeping only what a decision would use.

decision: What the class list leads with and how dense it is
options: Day-grouped rows: time, class name, teacher, spots left
Cards with a photo per class
Week grid calendar
recommendation: Day-grouped rows: time, class name, teacher, spots left
reason: One card recipe and a 16/26 body keep rows scannable at 390px with 44px tap targets, and the first view should be what she can book today.

decision: What a full class shows in the list and on its page
options: Shown as full, with the book button replaced by a quiet 'Full' label
Hidden from the list
Waitlist button with a join flow
recommendation: Shown as full, with the book button replaced by a quiet 'Full' label
reason: Her principle of shipping the smallest version that works end to end means no waitlist yet, and one filled button per view stays on the open classes.

decision: How 'Book your usual' appears on the class list
options: A single row above the list showing the usual class, with one verb-and-object button
A tab beside the class list
Leave it out until the first-time path is proven
recommendation: A single row above the list showing the usual class, with one verb-and-object button
reason: It branches straight from the list (n1 to n5) and skips the class and confirm steps, so it needs one clear spot; first-time visitors with no history see no row at all.

decision: Which single accent colour the page uses
options: Warm clay on paper, used only on the main button and spots-left tag
Sage green
Near-black only, no accent
recommendation: Warm clay on paper, used only on the main button and spots-left tag
reason: The interface stays 90 to 95% neutral with one accent per surface, and clay reads calm for a yoga studio and avoids violet.

note: Sketched the structure of the yoga booking page: what leads the class list, the full-class state, the "Book your usual" shortcut and the accent.

decision: What happens when two people take the last spot
options: First confirmed booking wins; the second sees 'class just filled' and is sent back to classes
Allow overbooking by one and let the studio sort it out
Hold the spot for a few minutes while the person confirms
recommendation: First confirmed booking wins; the second sees 'class just filled' and is sent back to classes
reason: A single atomic spot check at confirm is the plain, proven fix and needs no extra screens.

decision: Whether 'remember me on this device' is on, powering Book your usual
options: On: store name and email on the device only, and show Book your usual only when a past booking is saved
Off: remove Book your usual and make everyone retype details
On, with an account and login
recommendation: On: store name and email on the device only, and show Book your usual only when a past booking is saved
reason: Device-only storage keeps the usual shortcut working without accounts or a server-side profile to secure.

decision: What the page does when booking or the confirmation message fails
options: Show a plain error with Try again, keep the entered details, and never show 'booked' until the server confirms
Show 'booked' optimistically and retry in the background
Send the person to a phone or email contact page
recommendation: Show a plain error with Try again, keep the entered details, and never show 'booked' until the server confirms
reason: Telling someone they are booked when they are not is the costliest failure, so only the server's confirmation counts.

decision: What is collected and stored for each booking, and how it is confirmed
options: Name and email only, stored in one bookings table, with an email confirmation
Name, email and phone, with a text confirmation
Name only, with on-screen confirmation and no message
recommendation: Name and email only, stored in one bookings table, with an email confirmation
reason: The smallest data that still lets us send a confirmation keeps storage simple and the phone field switch off.

note: Engineering view of the yoga booking page: double booking, failure handling, stored data, and the "Book your usual" remember-me switch.

decision: Who 'Book your usual' serves and how it recognises a returning customer
options: Defer it until there is booking history to learn from
Remember the customer by email and offer their last class
Let them pick a saved favourite class
recommendation: Defer it until there is booking history to learn from
reason: It needs repeat-booking data to work and the first version should be proven end to end before adding a shortcut.
